Advertisement View all journals Saved research Search Account Log in Content Explore content About the journal Publish with us Subscribe Sign up for alerts RSS feed nature nature water perspectives article Perspective Published: 11 November 2026 Core AI ideas liberate our inquiry into the global water cycle Chaopeng Shen ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-0685-1901 1 & Yoshihide Wada ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-4770-2539 2 Nature Water ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 73 Accesses 1 Altmetric Metrics details Abstract The long-term value of artificial intelligence (AI) for water sciences remains the subject of debate. Here we argue that the core ideas underlying AI (rather than specific algorithms) can be integrated with domain knowledge to open new modes of scientific inquiry. We identify eight such core ideas, each offering capabilities difficult to achieve within traditional frameworks. Among these, expressive inductive bias allows architectures to declare what matters most while retaining capacity to learn the unexpected; differentiable programming enables constrained learning of partially known relationships; generative models capture joint distributions supporting conditional inference from fragmented observations; functional mapping learns solution operators providing orders-of-magnitude speedups for simulations; and inference-time computation enables AI to decompose complex problems. These ideas build on AI’s ability to learn useful representations of complex systems. Across many of them, a central mode of inquiry is ‘constrained learning’: posing unknown relationships as learnable components within known physical or conceptual frameworks. Tools built on these ideas can broaden access to reliable water predictions and support important open questions such as land–atmosphere interactions, organizing principles of the waterscape, groundwater sustainability, and human water-use behaviours. Domain insights can also feed back to advance general AI, benefiting the broader sciences.
